mainTopic: The source for the לאו against slaughtering an offering outside the עזרה: the ברייתא on ויקרא 17, רבי אבין's rejected קל וחומר, and רבי יוחנן's גזירה שוה.
overview: This amud finishes a ברייתא on ויקרא 17. Offerings consecrated and sacrificed after private altars (במות) were forbidden have both a punishment (כרת) and a warning (אזהרה). Offerings consecrated while במות were allowed but sacrificed outside after the ban get an עשה and a לא תעשה, but no כרת. Because the verse ולא יזבחו עוד is used for that special case, the גמרא needs another source for the general לאו against slaughtering outside. רבי אבין suggests a קל וחומר: if the lighter case is forbidden, surely the case with כרת is forbidden too. רבינא challenges this method from חלב, and רבא answers that every possible source for חלב has its own stringency, so the תורה had to write its לאו. רבא then raises a second challenge from פסח and מילה, which רב כהנא answers by pointing out that a missed פסח can be made up. Finally the גמרא rejects the method itself, since a warning can never be learned from a קל וחומר. It learns the warning instead from רבי יוחנן's גזירה שוה of 'bringing'–'bringing'.

steps.title: Proof that the earlier verses cover offerings consecrated and sacrificed during the prohibition
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא proves that the first section of verses is about offerings consecrated and sacrificed after במות were forbidden, because both the punishment and the warning for them are written.
steps.simpleTranslation: For their punishment is stated: "And to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting" (ending with כרת). The warning is written too: "Take heed lest you offer up your burnt offerings."
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא is finishing a point it started just before this section. It shows why the first verses must be about offerings consecrated and sacrificed during the time when במות were forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For offerings that were holy only after במות became forbidden, the תורה gives a full law. The punishment (כרת) comes from ויקרא 17:4, and the warning (אזהרה) comes from דברים 12:13. Since this case is fully covered, the ברייתא can now say that the later verses must be teaching something else.

keyTerms.meaning: Punishment; here, כרת for sacrificing outside
A warning; the verse that actually forbids the act
The Tent of Meeting, meaning the משכן
For, since; introduces a proof

steps.confusionAlert: The text starts in the middle of a sentence. "Their punishment" refers to the case the ברייתא described just before: offerings consecrated and sacrificed after במות became forbidden.

phrases.english: For their punishment is stated:
phrases.notes: "Their" points back to the case just before this: offerings consecrated and offered after private altars were forbidden.

phrases.english: "And to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 17:4. That verse ends by saying the person gets כרת.

phrases.english: and the warning: as it is written,
"Take heed to yourself lest you offer up your burnt offerings."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא's first section, which began before this text.
steps.raayaObject: That the first verses of the פרשה deal with offerings consecrated and sacrificed after במות were forbidden

steps.title: The later verses deal with offerings consecrated when private altars were allowed
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא states that from this point on, the verses discuss offerings consecrated while במות were permitted but sacrificed after they were forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: From here onward, the verses are about offerings that someone consecrated when private altars were allowed, and then sacrificed when private altars were forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא opens a new section and tells us what case the next verses are talking about. The proof comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a mixed case. The animal became holy at a time when sacrificing on a private altar was allowed, before the משכן stood. It was then offered after that became forbidden. The ברייתא says the תורה has a separate set of verses just for this situation.

keyTerms.meaning: From here onward
He consecrated, made holy for an offering
Private altars
Permitted time / forbidden time

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the ברייתא splits the פרשה into separate cases based on when the animal became holy.

phrases.english: From here onward,
phrases.notes: From this point on in the פסוקים of ויקרא 17.

phrases.english: it is about offerings that one consecrated
at a time when private altars were permitted
and sacrificed them at a time when private altars were forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the first case, the ברייתא moves to a second case covered by the later verses.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The later verses of the פרשה deal with offerings consecrated when במות were permitted and sacrificed when they were forbidden.

steps.title: Proof from the verse, and the meaning of "upon the open field"
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא reads "their sacrifices which they slaughter" as offerings already permitted before. It reads "upon the open field" as teaching that one who sacrifices during the prohibition is treated as if he sacrificed in an open field.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: "In order that the children of Israel shall bring their sacrifices which they slaughter." This means offerings I already permitted to you. "Upon the open field" tells you that one who sacrifices when private altars are forbidden is regarded by the verse as if he offered upon the open field.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא brings ויקרא 17:5 to prove that the verses are talking about offerings from the time when private altars were allowed. It also learns a lesson from the words "upon the open field."
steps.deeperAnalysis: "Which they slaughter" describes offerings people were already sacrificing, meaning ones that were permitted on a private altar before. So the verse is about animals consecrated during the permitted time. "Upon the open field" adds a harsh judgment: once private altars are forbidden, offering there is treated like offering out in a field, not a proper sacrifice.

keyTerms.meaning: Offerings I already permitted to you
Upon the open field
The verse regards him as if
To tell you; introduces what a word comes to teach

phrases.english: As it is said:
"In order that the children of Israel shall bring
their sacrifices which they slaughter":
offerings that I already permitted to you.
"Upon the open field":
this tells you
that one who sacrifices at a time when private altars are forbidden,
the verse regards him
as if he sacrificed upon the open field.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: לְמַעַן אֲשֶׁר יָבִיאוּ בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the case definition given in step 2.
steps.raayaObject: That the later verses deal with offerings consecrated while במות were permitted
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא 17:5, "their sacrifices which they slaughter" and "upon the open field"

steps.title: "And they shall bring them to ה׳" is a positive commandment
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא learns from "and they shall bring them to ה׳" that there is a positive commandment (עשה) to bring these offerings to the משכן.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And they shall bring them to ה׳": this is a positive commandment.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues reading the same verse. It finds a positive commandment to bring these earlier-consecrated offerings to the משכן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even an animal made holy back when private altars were allowed must now be brought to the משכן. That is the עשה. A prohibition has not been shown yet, and that is the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: And they shall bring them to ה׳
A positive commandment

phrases.english: "And they shall bring them to ה׳":
this is a positive commandment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues reading ויקרא 17:5 and draws a legal rule from it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a positive commandment to bring offerings consecrated during the permitted time to the משכן.

steps.title: Where is the prohibition for this case?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks where we learn that there is also a prohibition (לא תעשה) for this case.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know the prohibition?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks a question to set up the next step: it has an עשה, but where is the לא תעשה?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A positive commandment alone is not the same as a prohibition. The ברייתא wants to show that sacrificing these offerings outside also breaks a לא תעשה.

keyTerms.meaning: A prohibition, a negative commandment
From where do we know?

phrases.english: From where do we know the prohibition?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having found the עשה, the ברייתא asks for the לא תעשה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The verse that gives a prohibition for sacrificing earlier-consecrated offerings outside the משכן

steps.title: The prohibition comes from "and they shall not slaughter anymore"
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers that the prohibition comes from "and they shall not slaughter anymore" (ויקרא 17:7).
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse teaches: "And they shall not slaughter anymore."
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its question with ויקרא 17:7.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word "anymore" (עוד) shows that what used to be allowed is now forbidden. So offerings consecrated during the permitted time have both an עשה and a לא תעשה once private altars are forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse teaches
And they shall not slaughter anymore

steps.whatToRemember: For offerings consecrated when private altars were allowed but sacrificed after they were forbidden, the תורה gives an עשה ("and they shall bring them to ה׳") and a לא תעשה ("and they shall not slaughter anymore"). It also calls such sacrificing like offering "upon the open field."

phrases.english: The verse teaches:
"And they shall not slaughter anymore."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The prohibition comes from ויקרא 17:7, "and they shall not slaughter anymore."

steps.title: The ברייתא Rules Out the כרת Punishment
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks whether one who sacrifices these offerings outside is punished with כרת. It answers no, from "זאת להם": this is their punishment, and no other.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think he is punished with כרת. So the verse says: "This shall be an eternal statute to them for their generations." This is for them, and nothing else is for them.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes its teaching about offerings consecrated while במות were permitted. It says one who sacrifices them outside the משכן is not punished with כרת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse limits the punishment: "זאת" (this, the עשה and the לאו) applies to them, and no harsher punishment does. This shows that the whole passage, including ולא יזבחו עוד, is about this special case. So the גמרא will have to find a different source for the general לאו against slaughtering outside.

keyTerms.meaning: "One might think...": opens a possible idea that the ברייתא will reject
Spiritual cutting off, a severe punishment from Heaven
"The verse teaches": brings the פסוק that settles the question
An eternal statute

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think this ברייתא is about every offering slaughtered outside. Ordinary offerings slaughtered outside do carry כרת. This ברייתא only removes כרת from the special case of offerings consecrated while במות were permitted.
steps.whyThisMatters: Because ולא יזבחו עוד is tied to this special case, the general לאו needs another source. That sets up רבי אבין's קל וחומר.

phrases.english: One might think he would be punished with כרת?
phrases.notes: "He" is the person who sacrifices outside, after the ban, an offering he consecrated while במות were allowed.

phrases.english: The verse teaches:
"This shall be an eternal statute to them throughout their generations"
This is for them, and no other is for them.
phrases.notes: "This" means the עשה and לאו already mentioned, so no harsher punishment like כרת applies.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל יְהֵא עָנוּשׁ כָּרֵת? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא of steps 2-6 by setting the limit of the punishment for this special case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Offerings consecrated while במות were permitted and sacrificed outside after the ban carry an עשה and a לאו, but not כרת.

steps.title: רבי אבין Derives the Prohibition Through a קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: Since the verse is used up, רבי אבין learns the general לאו of slaughtering outside through a קל וחומר. If the Torah forbade the lighter case that has no punishment, surely it forbade the case that does have a punishment.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי אבין said: it is a קל וחומר. In a place where the Torah gave no punishment, it still gave a warning. In a place where it did give a punishment, isn't it logical that it gave a warning?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the idea that ולא יזבחו עוד is the source and gives a new one. רבי אבין uses a קל וחומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lighter case is the offering consecrated while במות were allowed: no כרת, yet the Torah forbids it. The stricter case is the ordinary offering slaughtered outside, which carries כרת. If the lighter case has a לאו, the stricter case must have one too.

keyTerms.meaning: A logical argument from a lighter case to a stricter case
The Torah gave a punishment
The Torah gave a warning, meaning it wrote a prohibition (לאו)
"Isn't it logical?": the closing words of a קל וחומר

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a general method: when the Torah gives a punishment, the prohibition can be learned by logic. The next step tests that method.

phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi Avin said:
It is a קל וחומר;
Just as in a place where He did not punish, He warned,
in a place where He did punish, isn't it logical that He warned?!
phrases.notes: The "place where He did punish" is an ordinary offering slaughtered outside, which carries כרת.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַבִּי אָבִין: קַל וָחוֹמֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the verse-based source, now limited by step 7, with a logical derivation.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source of the לאו against slaughtering an offering outside the Temple.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A קל וחומר from the special-case offering (no punishment, yet forbidden) to the ordinary case (has כרת, so surely forbidden).

steps.title: רבינא Challenges the Method Using Forbidden Fat
steps.stepSummary: רבינא asks רב אשי: if a punished act can learn its prohibition by קל וחומר, the Torah should not need a לאו for חלב. It could be learned from נבילה, which has a לאו but no כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רב אשי: If so, the Torah shouldn't need to state a לאו for חלב. Let it come by קל וחומר from נבילה: if נבילה, which has no punishment, has a warning, isn't it logical that חלב, which has a punishment, has a warning?
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא attacks רבי אבין's kind of reasoning. He points to a place where the Torah wrote out a לאו that this logic would make unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Eating נבילה is forbidden but carries no כרת. Eating חלב carries כרת. By רבי אבין's logic, the לאו for חלב should come from נבילה, yet the Torah writes it out. That suggests we don't learn prohibitions this way.

keyTerms.meaning: "If so": opens a challenge from where an argument would lead
A negative commandment, a prohibition
Forbidden fats of a kosher animal; eating them carries כרת
An animal that died without proper שחיטה; eating it is forbidden but carries no כרת

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rav Ashi:

phrases.aramaic: אִם כֵּן, לֹא יֵאָמֵר לָאו בְּחֵלֶב –
phrases.english: If so, let a prohibition not be stated regarding forbidden fat,
and let it come through a קל וחומר from a carcass:
Just as a carcass, for which He did not punish, He warned,
forbidden fat, for which He did punish, isn't it logical that He warned?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבִינָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי: אִם כֵּן, לֹא יֵאָמֵר לָאו בְּחֵלֶב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reasoning used by רבי אבין in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אבין's method of learning a prohibition by קל וחומר from a case without punishment to a case with punishment.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If that method worked, the Torah's written לאו for חלב would be unnecessary, since it could be learned from נבילה. A written לאו suggests the method is not used.

steps.title: רבא Shows Why the Carcass Comparison Fails
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the קל וחומר from נבילה does not work. נבילה has its own stringency, since it makes things טמא, so the Torah had to write the לאו for חלב.
steps.simpleTranslation: He came before רבא, and רבא said to him: It cannot be learned from נבילה either, because there is a refutation: what about נבילה? It is special, because it makes things טמא!
steps.whatsHappening: The question is brought to רבא, who answers רבינא's challenge. He shows that the חלב case is different, because its קל וחומר breaks down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קל וחומר only works if the lighter case is truly lighter in every way. נבילה is stricter than חלב in one way: it causes טומאה. So we can't say "if נבילה is forbidden, surely חלב is." That is why the Torah had to write the לאו for חלב, and רבי אבין's קל וחומר is not disproven.

keyTerms.meaning: "It comes": it can be learned or derived
To refute, to break down an argument by finding a difference
"What about X? It has a special feature": the standard form for refuting a קל וחומר
Makes things ritually impure (טמא)

steps.whatToRemember: A קל וחומר can be broken by any special stringency of the "lighter" case. נבילה makes things טמא, so it can't teach about חלב. That is why the Torah wrote the לאו for חלב, and רבי אבין's קל וחומר still stands.
steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying חלב has no לאו. The Torah clearly wrote one. He is explaining why the Torah had to write it out instead of leaving it to a קל וחומר.

phrases.english: He came before Rava, and Rava said to him:
phrases.notes: רב אשי brought רבינא's question to רבא.

phrases.english: It cannot be derived from a carcass either,
because it can be refuted:
What about a carcass? It is special, because it imparts impurity!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִנְּבֵלָה נָמֵי לָא אָתְיָא, דְּאִיכָּא לְמִיפְרַךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבינא's challenge in step 9, leaving רבי אבין's method from step 8 standing.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: the challenge's קל וחומר is refuted by a special stringency.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the Torah wrote a לאו for חלב, we might think a punishment never teaches a prohibition by קל וחומר.
steps.terutzMaskana: The חלב case is special because נבילה causes טומאה, which breaks that קל וחומר. Where no such refutation exists, as with רבי אבין's case, the קל וחומר works.

steps.title: Try learning חלב from impure creeping animals
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests learning the לאו of חלב by קל וחומר from שרצים טמאין, which have a לאו but no כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us learn it from impure creeping animals.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes a new attempt to learn the לאו of חלב by קל וחומר, this time from impure שרצים. It is setting up a proposal that will be tested right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נבילה failed as a source in step 10. So the גמרא looks for another prohibition that has a לאו but no כרת. If even the lighter שרצים are forbidden, then surely חלב, which carries כרת, is forbidden too.

keyTerms.meaning: Impure creeping animals, forbidden to eat, whose bodies make things טמא

phrases.english: From impure creeping animals.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After נבילה is rejected, a new candidate source for the קל וחומר is offered.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the Torah needed to write a לאו for חלב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If impure שרצים have a לאו without כרת, then חלב, which has כרת, should be forbidden by קל וחומר, and its לאו would be unnecessary.

steps.title: Impure creeping animals make things impure even in a tiny amount
steps.stepSummary: Rejected: impure שרצים are stricter in one way, since even a tiny amount of them makes things טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about impure creeping animals? They are special because they make things impure with even the tiniest amount!
steps.whatsHappening: The proposal is rejected. Impure שרצים have a stringency that חלב lacks, so you cannot reason from them to חלב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קל וחומר works only if the source is lighter than the target in every way. Impure שרצים make things טמא even with a tiny amount, which חלב does not do. So they are not truly 'lighter', and the קל וחומר falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What about...?': the standard way to point out that the source has its own stringency
They make things ritually impure
With any amount at all, even the tiniest bit

phrases.english: What about impure creeping animals?
They make things impure with any amount!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Refutes the proposal of step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Refuting the קל וחומר by pointing to the source's unique stringency.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Impure שרצים are lighter than חלב, so חלב could be learned from them.
steps.terutzMaskana: Impure שרצים make things טמא in any amount, so they are not lighter, and the לאו for חלב is still needed.

steps.title: Try learning חלב from pure creeping animals
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now suggests learning from pure שרצים, which do not make things טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us learn it from pure creeping animals.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a new source to get around the last rejection. Pure שרצים do not make things טמא, so the stringency from step 12 does not apply to them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The objection to impure שרצים was their power to make things טמא. Pure שרצים do not have that power, yet eating them is still forbidden without כרת. So the קל וחומר seems to work again.

keyTerms.meaning: Creeping animals that do not make things impure, yet are still forbidden to eat

phrases.english: From pure creeping animals.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new candidate chosen to avoid the stringency raised in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for a written לאו for חלב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Pure שרצים do not make things טמא and have no כרת, so חלב should be forbidden from them by קל וחומר.

steps.title: Pure creeping animals are forbidden even in a tiny amount
steps.stepSummary: Rejected: the prohibition of pure שרצים applies to any amount, while חלב needs a minimum amount.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about pure creeping animals? They are special because eating even the tiniest amount of them is forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: This source is rejected too. Pure שרצים have their own stringency: you are liable for eating any amount of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For חלב, a person is liable only for eating a set amount. For pure שרצים, even a tiny bit makes you liable. That makes them stricter in one way, so they cannot serve as the 'lighter' side of a קל וחומר.

keyTerms.meaning: Their prohibition

phrases.english: What about pure creeping animals?
Their prohibition applies to any amount!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Refutes the proposal of step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Refuting the קל וחומר by pointing to the source's unique stringency.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Pure שרצים have no stringency over חלב.
steps.terutzMaskana: They are forbidden in any amount, so the קל וחומר fails.

steps.title: Try learning חלב from ערלה and כלאי הכרם
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests ערלה and כלאי הכרם, which, like חלב, are only punished for a set amount.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us learn it from ערלה and כלאי הכרם.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries yet another source. ערלה and כלאי הכרם avoid the 'any amount' problem from step 14.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These prohibitions have a לאו but no כרת. They also do not apply to any tiny amount, so the last objection does not reach them. So the קל וחומר to חלב seems possible again.

keyTerms.meaning: Fruit of a tree in its first three years, which is forbidden
Forbidden mixed plantings in a vineyard

phrases.english: From ערלה and mixed plantings in a vineyard.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new candidate that avoids the stringency raised in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for a written לאו for חלב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: ערלה and כלאי הכרם have a לאו without כרת, so חלב should follow by קל וחומר.

steps.title: ערלה and כלאי הכרם are forbidden even for benefit
steps.stepSummary: Rejected: ערלה and כלאי הכרם are אסורין בהנאה, which חלב is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about ערלה and כלאי הכרם? They are special because you may not even get any benefit from them!
steps.whatsHappening: This source is also rejected. ערלה and כלאי הכרם are stricter because all benefit from them is forbidden, not just eating.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone may get benefit from חלב, for example by using it, even though eating it is forbidden. ערלה and כלאי הכרם forbid all benefit. So they are stricter in this way, and the קל וחומר fails.

keyTerms.meaning: Forbidden to get any benefit from, not only to eat

phrases.english: What about ערלה and mixed plantings in a vineyard?
For they are forbidden for benefit!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Refutes the proposal of step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Refuting the קל וחומר by pointing to the source's unique stringency.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ערלה and כלאי הכרם are lighter than חלב.
steps.terutzMaskana: They are אסורין בהנאה, so they are not lighter, and the קל וחומר fails.

steps.title: Try learning חלב from שביעית produce
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests שביעית produce, which may be used for benefit, just like חלב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us learn it from שביעית produce.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes another attempt. It picks שביעית produce, because benefit from it is allowed, so the objection from step 16 does not apply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem with ערלה was the ban on benefit. שביעית produce may be used for benefit, like חלב. So it looks like a fair 'lighter' source for the קל וחומר.

keyTerms.meaning: Produce of the seventh year (שמיטה), which has special holiness

phrases.english: From produce of the Sabbatical Year.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new candidate that avoids the stringency raised in step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for a written לאו for חלב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שביעית has a prohibition without כרת and allows benefit, so חלב should follow from it by קל וחומר.

steps.title: שביעית passes its holiness onto the money paid for it
steps.stepSummary: Rejected: שביעית is stricter because its holiness passes onto the money it is sold for.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about שביעית produce? It is special because it takes hold of the money paid for it!
steps.whatsHappening: This proposal is rejected too. שביעית has its own stringency: its holiness passes onto the money it is exchanged for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חלב has nothing like this. So far, every source tried has some stringency that חלב lacks, so no קל וחומר can be built from it. The next step tries one more source, תרומה.

keyTerms.meaning: It takes hold of its money, so its holiness passes onto the money it is sold for

steps.whatToRemember: So far, every attempt to learn the לאו of חלב by קל וחומר fails. Each source (נבילה, impure שרצים, pure שרצים, ערלה and כלאי הכרם, שביעית) has its own stringency. So the תורה had to write the לאו for חלב. This answers רבינא's challenge: the written לאו for חלב does not disprove רבי אבין's קל וחומר.
steps.confusionAlert: The goal is not to prove these sources are stricter than חלב overall. A קל וחומר breaks if the source is stricter in even one way.

phrases.english: What about Sabbatical Year produce?
For it takes hold of its money!
phrases.notes: When שביעית produce is sold, the money it brings in takes on its holiness.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Refutes the proposal of step 17. One more attempt (תרומה) follows.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Refuting the קל וחומר by pointing to the source's unique stringency.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שביעית, which allows benefit, is lighter than חלב.
steps.terutzMaskana: שביעית passes its holiness onto its money, so it is not lighter, and no source works for חלב.

steps.title: Suggesting תרומה as the source
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests learning the לאו of חלב from תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Maybe learn it from תרומה?
steps.whatsHappening: After rejecting שביעית, the גמרא tries one more source: תרומה, which a non-כהן may not eat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תרומה seems like a good match for חלב. It is a food prohibition, and it is not אסור בהנאה. Its holiness also does not pass onto money like שביעית does. So the earlier objections do not seem to apply here.

keyTerms.meaning: The portion of produce given to a כהן; a non-כהן may not eat it

phrases.english: From תרומה?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new suggested source after שביעית was rejected in Step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that no source can serve as a model for חלב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: תרומה avoids all the earlier objections, so maybe the לאו of חלב can be learned from it.

steps.title: תרומה has no permitted part
steps.stepSummary: Rejected: תרומה has no permitted part, unlike חלב, which is permitted in a wild animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because no part of it was ever permitted from its general rule.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects תרומה because it is stricter than חלב in one way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חלב is only forbidden in a בהמה (a domestic animal). The fat of a חיה (a wild animal) is permitted. תרומה has no such permitted part: the ban on non-כהנים covers all of it. So תרומה is stricter, and you cannot learn the weaker case of חלב from it.

keyTerms.meaning: Part of its general category was permitted

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean תרומה is permitted to anyone. It means no part of the תרומה category is ever permitted to a non-כהן, while some חלב (from a חיה) is fully permitted.

phrases.english: For no part of its general category was permitted!
phrases.notes: Compare חלב: the fat of a wild animal is permitted, so part of חלב's category is allowed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the תרומה suggestion from Step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: פירכא (pointing out what makes the source stricter)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: תרומה is a good model for חלב.
steps.terutzMaskana: תרומה is stricter because no part of it is permitted, so it cannot teach חלב.

steps.title: The same objection knocks out every source
steps.stepSummary: The same point rejects all the earlier sources too, since none of them has a permitted part.
steps.simpleTranslation: From all of them as well, one cannot learn it, because no part of their general category was permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says this one objection is enough to reject every source tried so far.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each earlier source was rejected for its own reason. Now the גמרא notes that one simple point covers all of them: נבילה, שרצים, ערלה, כלאי הכרם, שביעית and תרומה have no permitted part, while חלב does. So no קל וחומר from them can produce the לאו of חלב. The Torah had to write that לאו, and רבינא's challenge to רבי אבין falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: From all of them as well

steps.whatToRemember: חלב is unusual because part of it (the fat of a חיה) is permitted. That makes it 'weaker' than every other prohibition tried, so none of them can teach it through a קל וחומר.

phrases.english: From all of them, too,
phrases.notes: He means all the sources tried earlier in this discussion: נבילה, שרצים, ערלה, כלאי הכרם, שביעית.

phrases.english: for no part of their general category was permitted!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכּוּלְּהוּ נָמֵי שֶׁכֵּן לֹא הוּתְּרוּ מִכְּלָלָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands the objection from Step 20 to cover every earlier suggestion.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: No prohibition tried can serve as the model for חלב, because each has no permitted part and חלב does.

steps.title: רבא brings up the משנה about פסח and מילה
steps.stepSummary: רבא sets up his difficulty: a משנה lists פסח and מילה as positive commandments.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: If anything bothers me, this bothers me: what we learned in a משנה, that פסח and מילה are positive commandments.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא is preparing a challenge. He quotes the משנה that lists פסח and מילה as positive commandments (things you must do), not prohibitions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists sins that carry כרת. Most are prohibitions, but פסח and מילה stand out as מצות עשה. This means there is no לאו for skipping them. רבא will now show why that fact is a problem.

keyTerms.term: אִי קַשְׁיָא לִי הָא קַשְׁיָא לִי
keyTerms.meaning: If anything is difficult for me, this is
The קרבן פסח
Circumcision
A positive commandment, something one must do

phrases.english: רבא said:

phrases.aramaic: אִי קַשְׁיָא לִי הָא קַשְׁיָא לִי –
phrases.english: If anything is difficult for me, this is difficult for me:
That which we learned in a משנה:
פסח and מילה are positive commandments,

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי קַשְׁיָא לִי הָא קַשְׁיָא לִי הָא דִּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבא opens a second challenge to רבי אבין's קל וחומר from step 8: if that method worked, פסח and מילה should have a לאו.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה treats פסח and מילה as מצות עשה with no לאו.

steps.title: A קל וחומר from מותיר should give פסח a לאו
steps.stepSummary: רבא argues that a קל וחומר from מותיר should give פסח and מילה a לאו, which contradicts the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn it through a קל וחומר from מותיר: מותיר has no punishment, yet the תורה forbade it. פסח and מילה do have a punishment, so surely the תורה forbade them too!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives his challenge. If a קל וחומר could create a לאו, then פסח and מילה should have one, but the משנה says they don't.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Leaving over קרבן meat (מותיר) has a לאו even though it has no punishment. Skipping פסח or מילה carries כרת, which is a serious punishment. So by קל וחומר they should certainly have a לאו. The משנה calls them only מצות עשה, which suggests we do not create a לאו through a קל וחומר.

keyTerms.meaning: An argument from a lighter case to a stricter case
One who leaves over קרבן meat past its time
The תורה gave a punishment
The תורה gave a warning, meaning a לאו

steps.whyThisMatters: This challenges the idea that a לאו can be learned from a קל וחומר, which was the basis for trying to derive these prohibitions through a קל וחומר.

phrases.english: Let it be derived through a קל וחומר from one who leaves over:
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:30, the command not to leave קרבן meat until morning.

phrases.english: Just as with one who leaves over, where the תורה gave no punishment, it still forbade it,
פסח and מילה, where the תורה did give a punishment,
is it not logical that it forbade them?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the משנה from Step 22 to build the challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that a לאו can be created through a קל וחומר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a קל וחומר could create a לאו, פסח and מילה would get a לאו from מותיר. The משנה calls them only מצות עשה, so it seems a קל וחומר cannot create a לאו.

steps.title: רב כהנא: the קל וחומר from מותיר fails
steps.stepSummary: The קל וחומר is broken: מותיר cannot be fixed, but a missed פסח can be made up on פסח שני.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: I told this discussion to רב כהנא, and he said to me: It cannot be learned from מותיר, because there is a refutation. מותיר has no way to fix it. Would you say the same about פסח, which does have a fix?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי reports that רב כהנא answered רבא's question. The קל וחומר from מותיר does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once meat is left over, the sin can never be undone. That makes מותיר stricter in one way. A person who misses פסח can bring it on פסח שני, so פסח is lighter in that way. Since מותיר is stricter, it cannot teach a לאו to פסח, and the משנה no longer poses a problem.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a way to refute it
A fix or remedy
A teaching or discussion

steps.whatToRemember: A קל וחומר fails if the source case is stricter in any way. מותיר cannot be fixed, while פסח has פסח שני, so no לאו is learned for פסח.

phrases.english: רב אשי said:
I said this discussion before רב כהנא,
and he said to me: It cannot be derived from one who leaves over,
for there is a refutation:

phrases.aramaic: מָה לְמוֹתִיר – שֶׁכֵּן אֵין לוֹ תַּקָּנָה,
phrases.english: What about one who leaves over? He has no remedy,
would you say the same of פסח, which has a remedy?
phrases.notes: The remedy is פסח שני: someone who missed the first פסח brings it a month later.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's challenge from Step 23 by breaking the קל וחומר.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: פסח and מילה should get a לאו by קל וחומר from מותיר.
steps.terutzMaskana: מותיר is stricter because it cannot be fixed, so the קל וחומר fails, and the משנה's wording is no problem.

steps.title: A warning cannot be learned from a קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the whole idea of deriving a לאו through a קל וחומר. Even those who punish based on a קל וחומר agree that a warning cannot come from one.
steps.simpleTranslation: But can we really learn a warning from a logical argument? Even the opinion that allows punishing based on a logical argument agrees that we cannot learn a warning from one!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא steps back and attacks the method itself: you cannot learn a warning (לאו) from a קל וחומר at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier back-and-forth tried to use a קל וחומר to supply a לאו. The גמרא now says that even the lenient opinion, which lets a court punish based on a קל וחומר, admits that a warning must come from a real source in the Torah. So the קל וחומר approach falls apart completely, and a new source is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: We derive a warning (a prohibition, לאו)
We give a punishment
From a logical argument (here, a קל וחומר)
A Torah warning (prohibition) that must come before a punishment

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two halves. Some opinions allow a punishment to be learned from a קל וחומר, but everyone agrees a warning cannot be learned that way.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a basic rule: a לאו must come from an actual Torah source, not from reasoning alone. That is why the גמרא has to find a new way to get the warning.

phrases.english: But can one derive a warning from a logical inference?!
Even according to the one who says
that one punishes based on a logical inference,
one does not derive a warning from a logical inference!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the specific קל וחומר was answered in step 24, the גמרא now rejects the whole method of getting a לאו from a קל וחומר.
steps.kashyaTarget: The approach of deriving the לאו for שחוטי חוץ through a קל וחומר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A warning can never be derived from a קל וחומר, even according to the opinion that allows punishment to be derived from one.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's גזירה שוה from the word 'bringing'
steps.stepSummary: Instead of a קל וחומר, the warning for slaughtering outside is learned through a גזירה שוה. Offering up outside and slaughtering outside both use the word 'bringing,' so just as the Torah warned before punishing in one case, it did so in the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is like רבי יוחנן, who said: we learn it from the word 'bringing' here and 'bringing' there. Just as there the Torah did not punish unless it first warned, so too here, it did not punish unless it first warned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new, valid source for the warning: a גזירה שוה from רבי יוחנן, based on the same word 'bringing' appearing in both cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גזירה שוה is a real Torah source, so unlike a קל וחומר it can teach a warning. Offering up outside (להלן) has both a punishment and a warning. Slaughtering outside (כאן) has a stated punishment, so the shared word 'bringing' teaches that it must also carry a warning, even though none is written openly.

keyTerms.meaning: Learning one law from another because the Torah uses the same word in both places
'Bringing,' the shared word ('did not bring it to the entrance of the אהל מועד')
'There,' the case being learned from (offering up outside)
'Here,' the case being learned about (slaughtering outside)
Slaughtering a קרבן outside the עזרה

steps.whatToRemember: A קל וחומר cannot create a warning, so the לאו for שחוטי חוץ comes from רבי יוחנן's גזירה שוה of 'bringing'–'bringing': just as offering up outside has a warning along with its punishment, so does slaughtering outside.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the rule that the Torah does not punish without first warning, and that a גזירה שוה, unlike a קל וחומר, can supply that warning.

phrases.english: Rather, it is in accordance with Rabbi Yoḥanan,
who said: it is derived from 'bringing' and 'bringing';
phrases.notes: ויקרא 17:4 and 17:9: both slaughtering outside and offering up outside say 'and he did not bring it.'

phrases.english: just as there, the Torah did not punish
phrases.notes: 'There' is offering up outside, and 'here' is slaughtering outside.

phrases.english: unless it had warned,
so too here, it did not punish
unless it had warned.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא כִּדְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, דְּאָמַר: אָתְיָא הֲבָאָה–הֲבָאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Once the קל וחומר method is rejected in step 25, this step supplies a valid replacement source.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replacing the rejected source with a different method of derivation (a גזירה שוה).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The warning for שחוטי חוץ was to be learned through a קל וחומר.
steps.terutzMaskana: The warning is learned through רבי יוחנן's גזירה שוה of 'bringing'–'bringing' from offering up outside, which has both warning and punishment.
